chunks: He said, and Ali ibn Hassan narrated to me, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
Cause the sustenance to descend by charity.

key_terms.اسْتَنْزِلُوا: Imperative verb meaning 'cause to descend' or 'draw down' — used in the sense of inviting divine provision from above
key_terms.الرِّزْقَ: Rizq — divinely apportioned sustenance, encompassing both material provision (food, wealth) and spiritual sustenance
key_terms.الصَّدَقَةِ: Sadaqa — voluntary charity or almsgiving, distinct from the obligatory zakat; a key spiritual practice in Islamic tradition

ai.seo_question: How does charity (sadaqa) attract sustenance (rizq) according to the Imams?
ai.summary: The Imam (peace be upon him) instructs the faithful to draw down divine provision through the act of giving charity. This short but powerful teaching reflects the belief, well-established in both the Quran and hadith, that sadaqa (voluntary almsgiving) is not merely a moral duty but a spiritual mechanism for attracting God's blessings and ensuring material well-being. The community receiving this instruction understood sadaqa as a direct means of invoking divine generosity.

en.hubeali:
He said, ‘And it has been narrated to me by Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
Cause the sustenance to descend by the charity’.
en.sarwar: 4. The narrator of the above Hadith has said that Ali ibn Hassan narrated to me from Musa ibn Bakr who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Make the means of sustenance descend to you by giving charity.’”
